_disabledMcpServers._resolved_2026_09_07: Both fantastical and monarch-money were disabled here earlier on 2026-09-07 and have since been FIXED and re-enabled below. Keeping the causes recorded because both were misdiagnosed at first and both are the same failure CLASS -- an upstream returning a malformed JSON-RPC error that mcpx's main() does not catch, killing the whole gateway (supervisord then hits startretries=3 and stops mcpx-server permanently, while the Docker healthcheck keeps reporting healthy because it probes the UI on :5173, not :9000). FANTASTICAL: not a flaky process as first written here -- supergateway 3.4.3's stdioToSse reuses ONE MCP SDK Server across SSE sessions and overwrites sseTransport.onclose AFTER server.connect(), so Protocol._transport is never released. With @modelcontextprotocol/sdk >= 1.26.0 the second connect() throws 'Already connected to a transport', uncaught. That is ONE SSE session per process lifetime -- sequential connects fail exactly like concurrent ones (verified on a fresh process: session A OK, closed, session B 2.5s later FAILED). launchd KeepAlive respawned it 100,022 times / 335,704 logged crashes / 421MB of logs between 2026-07-01 and 2026-09-07. Fixed by pinning supergateway@3.3.0 (the one release with a per-session Server + pooled child) with --minConcurrency 1 --maxConcurrency 2 in mcps/fantastical/com.bobthearsonist.fantastical-mcp.plist. MONARCH: expired cookies were NOT the cause -- tools/list never touches credentials. mcp-proxy 0.12.0 holds one shared upstream stdio ClientSession, and that session died 2026-08-31 ~17:11 while the child process stayed alive and sleeping, so every forwarded method returned ErrorData(code=0, message='') from mcp/server/lowlevel/server.py:788. Fixed by restarting the monarch-money-mcp container. The cookies ARE separately dead (keyring dated 2026-05-31, verified 401) which breaks tool CALLS but not listing -- re-seed per docs/monarch-money-cookie-automation.md. Also corrected in this pass: mcps/mcpx/app.yaml's personal-finance group was using "*" on the false premise that the server ran without --enable-write, exposing all 39 tools including delete_account; it now carries an explicit 22-tool read list.
